UK’s MFS owner says he’s been harassed by lawsuits after US$3 bil collapse
article:
(Oct 8): The owner of Market Financial Solutions Ltd (MFS) is facing a growing barrage of lawsuits as creditors try to recover about £2.3 billion (US$3 billion) of loans they had extended to the UK property company that collapsed amid allegations of widespread fraud.

Paresh Raja is under pressure to respond to as many as six lawsuits relating to the collapse of Market Financial Solutions, or MFS, his lawyers said in a filing in one of the UK High Court cases. With creditors pursuing overlapping claims and battling among themselves, Raja has urged them to coordinate their efforts and combine at least some of the proceedings.

Creditors including Barclays plc and Apollo Global Management Inc’s Atlas SP Partners unit backed the sprawling group of entities that made up MFS. Many of those entities are now in administration, a UK form of insolvency, and seeking to recover funds through litigation. Some have accused Raja of looting the company of hundreds of millions of dollars and using proceeds of their loans to fund an extravagant lifestyle.

“These entities have made no effort whatsoever to coordinate these proceedings,” Raja’s lawyers wrote in the filing. “Indeed, there appears to be a significant degree of internecine warfare, the effect of which has been to harass Mr Raja at every stage with increasingly ‘urgent’ applications and across a range of fora, as each entity seeks to get what it evidently perceives to be ‘ahead’ of the others.”

Officials winding down MFS itself have sued Raja for £1.3 billion in a separate case. In his first detailed response to allegations of wrongdoing, Raja last month said he hadn’t “acted dishonestly or in bad faith at any time”. MFS was heading for a sale or an initial public offering before Barclays triggered its collapse by freezing key accounts, he claimed.

One of the MFS entities was London Bridging Ltd, or LBL, which was backed by loans from Barclays and Castlelake LP, an investment firm majority owned by Brookfield Asset Management Ltd. LBL has alleged that Raja “misappropriated” more than £200 million.

See also: Google accused of overcharging 20 mil consumers in UK class action

Raja has sought to suspend LBL’s case against him pending the resolution of various actions in other litigation, legal filings show. LBL has accused Raja of trying to “delay and/or avoid facing” its claims.

Two other MFS entities, Amber Bridging Ltd and Zircon Bridging Ltd, have indicated that they will issue claims against Raja “shortly”, his lawyers wrote in the filing this week. These entities, which borrowed more than £1 billion, may recover as little as nine to 13 pence on the pound for creditors including Apollo’s Atlas unit, early estimates show.

A spokesperson for AlixPartners, which is managing the administration of MFS, Amber and Zircon, declined to comment.

See also: UK expected to follow EU with China EV tariffs, report says

Administrators for one entity called Market Financial Solutions International Ltd, or MFSI, have “served statutory demands” — a formal request for payment — against Raja for £278 million. A separate entity called Interlend Holdings Ltd wrote to Raja’s lawyers earlier this month “demanding immediate payment” of £28 million.

“The various claimants are not coordinating their claims,” Raja’s lawyers wrote. “Instead, they are instead advancing competing, and overlapping and/or inconsistent, claims to what appears to be the same pool of money.”

Stephen Katz, an official at insolvency firm BTG Begbies Traynor, who’s overseeing the administration of MFSI and Interlend, didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

title: TCS profit beats estimates as IT deals start trickling in
article:
(Oct 8): Tata Consultancy Services Ltd (TCS) reported quarterly profit that topped analysts’ estimates, helped by cost-cutting measures and a gradually improving contract flow that helped drive growth at Asia’s largest IT services provider.

Net income rose 15% to 138.84 billion rupees in the three months through September, the company said in a statement on Thursday. Analysts expected 137.86 billion rupees on average. Sales climbed 11% to 731.88 billion rupees, helped by a decline in the Indian rupee versus the dollar and the euro.

TCS’ major customers in the US and Europe and remain cautious with large IT projects, with geopolitical tensions and elevated inflation weighing on economic growth. At the same time, artificial intelligence (AI) threatens to disrupt the traditional outsourcing business model of TCS and Indian peers such as Infosys Ltd.

As AI tools from OpenAI and Anthropic PBC begin to reshape how clients procure software services, TCS’ traditional recipe for success — hiring armies of graduates to write code for clients such as Apple Inc, Boeing Co and Bank of America Corp — is under pressure. While the company has sought to harness AI for its own purposes, investors remain sceptical — the stock has lost half its value over the past two years.

TCS has also embarked on a massive cost-cutting drive. Natarajan Chandrasekaran, chairman of TCS parent Tata Group, predicted in June that AI agents would make up half the company’s workforce in the future. But he was also quick to add that AI will open up fresh opportunities.

See also: Samsung profit up almost nine-fold with memory chip windfall

Mumbai-based TCS has also rapidly expanded its AI operations, saying annualised AI revenue reached US$3.1 billion in the quarter. Examples include two recent deals with AI components: earlier this month, TCS announced it will bring US consumer electronics retailer Best Buy Co’s India global capability centre into its fold, and in August it signed a €1.25 billion deal with Porsche AG for deploying AI, while also agreeing to buy its consulting unit.

The agreements with Porsche and Best Buy “represent a new category of transformation partnerships,” Chief executive officer K Krithivasan said in a statement. “Together with our clients, we are building repeatable value platforms that will industrialize AI at scale.”

TCS has also partnered with OpenAI to build AI data centres and is in similar discussions with other tech giants. India is expected to need about 10 gigawatts of AI data centre capacity over the next four years, and much of that is yet to be built. TCS is seeking to capitalise on the opportunity, Krithivasan has said.

See also: DeepSeek to raise at least US$12 bil in Tencent-backed funding

"Accenture, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, Capgemini, Cognizant and HCL Tech’s calendar 2Q results reinforce our thesis that a meaningful IT spending recovery is slipping towards 2027. Rising AI activity isn’t yet enough to offset slow enterprise decision-making. Financial services is the clearest bright spot, supported by demand for modernisation and AI with tangible returns," says Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Tamlin Bason.

India’s US$280 billion software services sector, led by TCS, began by offering cheap back office solutions to large international corporations, but they now provide a range of cloud, automation and AI services to multinationals including Citigroup Inc and PepsiCo Inc. That’s made the Indian IT giants direct rivals to global technology services providers from Accenture plc to International Business Machines Corp.

title: Seatrium wins FSRU conversion contract from Excelerate Energy
article:
Mainboard-listed Seatrium has won a contract for a floating storage regasification unit (FSRU) conversion project from Excelerate Energy. The deal includes an option for a second contract.

The scope of work includes engineering, procurement, construction, installation and commissioning spanning regasification facilities, LNG transfer and cargo handling systems, utility and offloading systems, electrical and automation systems, marine modifications, and associated infrastructure.

Alvin Gan, executive vice president of repairs and upgrades at Seatrium, says that Seatrium will leverage its deep engineering expertise and proven track record to convert the vessel into “critical” LNG infrastructure. “As demand for secure and lower carbon solutions continues to grow, we see a significant role Seatrium can play in offering scalable, cost-effective solutions to strengthen LNG value chains worldwide,” he adds.

Work is expected to commence in the current quarter, with an estimated delivery in 2028. Once completed, the FSRU will combine 170,000 cubic metres of LNG storage capacity, tri-fuel diesel electric power generation and reliquefaction technology to enhance asset performance and expand the range of opportunities it can serve, says Seatrium.

David Liner, executive vice president and COO of Excelerate Energy describes the project as an “important investment” in the continued growth of the company’s infrastructure portfolio and its ability to deliver “reliable” downstream LNG infrastructure to customers globally. “Upon completion, the vessel will become the 13th FSRU in our fleet and will expand the reach and capabilities of our LNG infrastructure platform,” says Liner.

The Excelerate contract marks Seatrium’s second publicly-announced FSRU award since CEO Chris Ong shared the firm’s goal to take a “leading share” of gas conversion projects at its 1HFY2026 results briefing on July 31. From the firm’s presentation slides, the pipeline for gas-related business totals around $11 billion, with Ong sharing that it is currently exploring “six to nine” FSRU tenders.

See also: ISOTeam wins new contracts worth $30.2 mil

Sharing that the offshore and marine giant is seeing rising demand for floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) and FSRU deployments, Ong adds that the company is well-positioned to seize opportunities in gas due to its market-leading capabilities, which include delivering the world’s only two operational liquefied natural gas carrier (LNGC) to FLNG conversions.

So far, Seatrium has executed 22 FSRU, FLNG and floating storage unit (FSU) conversion projects since 2007. It has developed FLNG-X, a proprietary, modular, and scalable newbuild FLNG design.

Shares of Seatrium closed at $1.96 on Oct 8, down 21 cents or 9.7% ytd. The company announced a $200 million share buyback programme on Sept 22 which gave its share price a temporary bounce.

See also: CSE Global secures two major electrification contracts in US worth $190.5 mil

However, worries over higher US interest rates, ballooning US debt, escalating energy prices and sustained geopolitical tension have been weighing down markets broadly, with Seatrium not escaping the negative sentiment.

In addition, analysts have also expressed concern over Seatrium’s orderbook replenishment. In particular, Terence Khi from JP Morgan has rated Seatrium “underweight” with a $1.60 valuation in his July 29 report.

In contrast, CGSI analysts Meghana Kande and Lim Siew Khee retain their optimism in the stock with a “buy” rating at $2.60 in their Aug 24 report.
